objective: Test whether the lab candidate C6 holds on held-out fixtures it was not designed on.
current_unknown: Whether C6's synthetic pass (designed and scored on the same 24 fixtures) is overfitted.
hypothesis: C6 keeps silent error rate <= 0.0336 and false-alarm rate <= 0.05 on 16 held-out fixtures.
competing_hypotheses: Rules R and E were tuned by looking at the decision fixtures and will not generalise.

stages.output: Held-out fixtures and decision rule committed in bd097c3 before any tracker ran on them.
16/16 held-out fixtures FIXTURE_ACCEPTED; 56/56 earlier fixtures bit-identical after adding the weak-cue variant.
C1 and C6 on 16 held-out fixtures, 277 s wall.
Held-out generalisation attack: C6 failed both pre-registered limits (silent 0.047, false alarms 0.112).
Fixture generator unchanged for all 56 earlier fixtures.
Rule R degrades when a track has several irregular bars; ho_two_odd causes 45/58 false alarms and 18/28 silent errors. C6 still beats C1 on silent errors, coverage and cost.
Real-track evidence (GRID-METER-003) now decisive; any track-level fail-closed rule must be pre-registered and tested on a new held-out set.

attacks.relevance: Held-out irregular-bar patterns not seen during rule design.
attacks.detail: C6 silent 28/595, false alarms 58/520; two odd bars in one track break rule R.

regression_check.detail: C6 silent error rate 0.0061 on designed-on fixtures vs 0.0471 held out: the earlier pass does not generalise.

limitations: Synthetic fixtures only, one timbre family.
Single tracker checkpoints; CPU time is a container proxy.

next_recommended_experiment.reason: Whether multi-odd-bar tracks are common in a real DJ library decides whether C6's held-out weakness matters.

human_interventions: GRID-METER-003 needs real tracks and listener verification.
